 Judgment

This Criminal Appeal under Section 374(2) of Cr.P.C. has been filed against judgment and sentence dated 26.04.2005 passed by Session Judge, Narsinghpur in Session Trial No.85/2004 by which appellant has been convicted under Section 506 Part-II of IPC.
2.
The facts necessary for disposal of present appeal in short are that on 18.02.2004 prosecutrix gave birth to a child.

sentences.text: On an inquiry it was found that by making a promise of marriage, appellant had committed rape on her and had also threatened her not to narrate the incident to anybody otherwise she will be killed.
Accordingly, the offence was registered.
Prosecutrix and accused were got medically examined.
The statements of witnesses were recorded.
Police after completing the investigation filed the charge sheet for offence under Sections 376, 506 of IPC.
3. Trial Court by order dated 15.07.2004 framed the charges under Sections 376, 506 Part-II of IPC.
4. Appellant abjured his guilt and pleaded not guilty.

5. The prosecution in order to prove its case examined prosecutrix (P.W.-1), father of prosecutrix (P.W.-2), Ajay Dubey (P.W.-3), Satyanarayan Jhariya (P.W.-4), Balkibai (P.W.-5), P.D. Pandey (P.W.-
6), Dr. K. Uikey (P.W.-7) and Bhupendra Singh Sengar (P.W.-8).
6. Appellant did not examine any witness in his defense.
7. Trial Court by impugned judgment and sentence dated 26.04.2005 acquitted the appellant for offence under Section 376 of IPC but convicted under Section 506 Part-II of IPC.
Trial Court came to a conclusion that on the date of FIR i.e. 18.02.2004 prosecutrix was aged about 18 years because as per the school record her date of birth was 06.10.1985.
Trial Court also came to a conclusion that prosecution has failed to prove that appellant had committed rape on the prosecutrix.

In nutshell,
the finding of Trial Court is that prosecutrix was a consenting party.

However, Trial Court has held that since appellant had extended a threat that in case if the incident is narrated to anybody then he will kill her, therefore, he is liable to punish under Section 506 Part II of IPC.

8. Challenging the judgment and sentence passed by the Court below, it is submitted by counsel for appellant that appellant had already remained in jail for approximately 2 months and 27 days whereas he has been awarded jail sentence of one year.
Accordingly, it is prayed that although appellant does not wish to challenge his conviction but he may be sentenced to the period already undergone by him.
9. Per contra, the appeal is vehemently opposed by counsel for State.

10. Heard learned counsel for parties.
11.
It is true that legal maxim falsus in uno, falsus in omnibus has no application in our country and the Court must make an effort to remove the chaff from grain.
However, if the evidence of prosecutrix is considered, then it is clear that Trial Court has already held that prosecutrix appears to be a consenting party.
Once there was no resistance by prosecutrix and she was the consenting party, then there is no question of extending a threat.
The prosecutrix has stated that petitioner had kept a knife and had extended a threat to her life but if she was a consenting party, then there was no question of extending any threat.

sentences.text: Under these circumstances, this Court is of considered opinion that Trial Court committed a material mistake by holding that any threat to the life of prosecutrix was ever extended by appellant.
Therefore, her evidence to that effect is held to be unreliable.

Under these circumstances, appellant is acquitted of the charge under Section 506 Part II of IPC.
13.

Ex- consequenti, the judgment and sentence dated 26.04.2005 passed by Session Judge,
Narsinghpur in Session Trial No.85/2004 is hereby set aside.
14. The bail bonds and surety bonds of appellant are hereby discharged.
15. Appellant is no more required in the present case.

16. Let a copy of this judgment alongwith record of Trial Court be sent back for necessary information and compliance.
17.
The appeal succeeds and is hereby allowed.
